info.name: OpenCred Server (Docker)
info.description:
HTTP requests for the OpenCred Docker image (`apps/server`). Targets the `/v1/*` API surface.

## How to use

1. Start the container locally (or via SSH tunnel if it's on a remote VM):
   ```
   docker run -d --name opencred -p 3100:3100 \
     -e OPENCRED_API_KEY="$OPENCRED_API_KEY" \
     -e OPENCRED_KEY_PATH=/secrets/issuer-key.pem \
     -v $PWD/keys/issuer-key.pem:/secrets/issuer-key.pem:ro \
     opencred:bootcamp
   ```
2. In Postman, edit the collection variables (Variables tab):
   - `baseUrl` — default `http://localhost:3100`
   - `apiKey` — paste the value of `OPENCRED_API_KEY`
3. Run **Public → GET /v1/health** to confirm `signingKeyLoaded: true`.
4. Run **Inspect → GET /v1/keys** — it auto-saves `issuerDid` into the collection variables for the issue requests.
5. Run **Issue & Verify → POST /v1/credentials/issue (vc-jwt)** — it auto-saves the response into `lastCredential` for the verify request.
6. Run **Issue & Verify → POST /v1/credentials/verify**.

Authentication is set at the collection level (Bearer `{{apiKey}}`); the two public endpoints override to no auth.

The response `credential` is a JSON-LD VC object whose `proof.jwt` holds the compact JWS.

Auto-saves the response into `{{lastCredential}}` for the verify request.

request.description:
Issue a credential against a JSON Schema you paste in the request body — no need for the schema to be in the bundled registry. The server compiles the schema, validates `credentialSubject` against it, and writes the schema's `$id` (or a base64 data-URI fallback) into the credential's `credentialSchema` block.

When `inlineSchema` is provided, `schemaId` becomes optional. If both are passed, the inline schema wins for validation and `credentialSchema.id`.

exec: // vc-jwt: credential is a JSON-LD object whose proof.jwt holds the
//   compact JWS — the verify endpoint wants just that JWT string.
// sd-jwt-vc: credential is already a compact ~-delimited string.
// data-integrity: credential is the JSON-LD VC; stringify wholesale.
// Save the full VC envelope (object form) so revocation-hash and
// package requests can pull the JSON-LD shape without re-parsing.
// When `revocationRegistryUrl` is set on the issue request, the
// server embeds the per-credential SHA-256 hash as the LAST URL
// segment of `credential.credentialStatus.id`. Extract it so the
// /credentials/revoke request has the right hash auto-threaded —
// no separate /revocation-hash call needed for OpenCred-issued VCs.

request.description:
Issue a Beckn-flavored electricity-customer credential (`schemaId: electricity/v1`) with **all five `credentialSubject` profile blocks** populated (`customerProfile`, `customerDetails`, `consumptionProfile`, `generationProfile`, `storageProfile`) and a DeDi-backed `credentialStatus` via `revocationRegistryUrl`.

Three friction points to watch for:

- `installationAddress.country` (and `city`, `state`) is `{ name?, code }`, where `code` matches ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`^[A-Z]{2}$`). Not a bare string.
- All date fields in this schema are `date-time` (full ISO 8601 with timezone), not `date`. Applies to `serviceConnectionDate`, `commissioningDate`, etc.
- Enums everywhere: `meterType` (`AMR | AMI | Electromechanical | Forward | Reverse | Bidirectional | Prepaid | NetMeter | Other`), `premisesType`, `connectionType`, `generationType`, `storageType`.

`proofFormat: vc-jwt` is required — `data-integrity` against this schema currently returns `CRYPTO_ERROR: Invalid JSON-LD syntax; tried to redefine a protected term` (tracked as opencred#596).

Only `customerProfile` is required under `credentialSubject`; the other four blocks are optional but populated here so you can demo the full schema in one click.

**Update the `revocationRegistryUrl`** to your DeDi instance's canonical lookup URL: `https://<host>/dedi/lookup/<namespace>/vc-revocation-registry`. The server stamps this verbatim into `credentialStatus.statusListCredential` and appends the per-credential SHA-256 hash to make `credentialStatus.id`.

**Auto-threading**: the post-test script saves the JWT string into `{{lastCredential}}`, the full VC object into `{{lastFullCredential}}`, AND extracts the revocation hash from `credentialStatus.id` into `{{lastRevocationHash}}`. Click straight to **Revocation (DeDi) → POST /v1/credentials/revoke**; no separate hash call needed.

exec: // Extract per-credential revocation hash from credentialStatus.id (the
// server appends the hash as the last URL segment when revocationRegistryUrl
// is set). Auto-threads lastRevocationHash for the /revoke request.

request.description:
When `revocationRegistryUrl` is set, the server attaches a `credentialStatus` block of type `dedi` and generates a `urn:uuid:` credential id. The per-credential SHA-256 hash is embedded as the LAST URL segment of `credentialStatus.id`.

Use the canonical DeDi lookup URL — `https://<host>/dedi/lookup/<namespace>/vc-revocation-registry` — so the credential is self-describing for W3C-compliant verifiers.

**Auto-threading**: the post-test script saves `{{lastCredential}}`, `{{lastFullCredential}}`, and `{{lastRevocationHash}}` (extracted from `credentialStatus.id`) — click straight to **Revocation (DeDi) → POST /v1/credentials/revoke** next.

One-call issue + package. The same `customization` knobs documented on `/v1/credentials/package` apply here. The response shape:

```json
{
  "credential": { ... },
  "proofFormat": "vc-jwt",
  "isCompactToken": false,
  "packagedOutputs": [
    { "format": "qr-png", "data": "data:image/png;base64,...", "encoding": "utf-8" },
    { "format": "qr-svg", "data": "<svg ...>", "encoding": "utf-8" },
    { "format": "pdf",    "data": "JVBERi0...", "encoding": "base64" },
    { "format": "json",   "data": "{ ... }", "encoding": "utf-8" }
  ]
}
```

Works with `proofFormat: "data-integrity"` and `"sd-jwt-vc"` too — for sd-jwt-vc the QR embeds the raw compact token verbatim.

exec: // Build the verify body programmatically from {{lastCredential}}.
// Why a pre-request script: the issue endpoint returns `credential`
// as either a string (vc-jwt, sd-jwt-vc) or an object (data-integrity).
// The post-response scripts on the issue requests JSON.stringify the
// object form, so {{lastCredential}} is always a string. But naive
// the JSON-stringified object contains literal `"` characters which
// terminate the surrounding string early and produce malformed JSON
// (the server returns 400 INVALID_JSON in that case).
// JSON.stringify on the value handles both forms uniformly — it
// produces a properly-escaped JSON string literal for embedding.
console.warn('lastCredential is empty — run an issue request first.');
const body = JSON.stringify({ credential: stored ?? '' }, null, 2);

request.description:
Verify any of the three proof formats — the server auto-detects. The `credential` field is a string: a JSON-stringified VC for data-integrity, or the compact token for vc-jwt and sd-jwt-vc.

The body is built programmatically by a **pre-request script** that reads `{{lastCredential}}` and JSON-encodes it safely. This works whether the credential came from `data-integrity` (object → stringified, contains `"`), `vc-jwt`, or `sd-jwt-vc`. The literal `"raw"` shown in Postman's body editor is overwritten before the request is sent — it's only there for documentation.

`{{lastCredential}}` is set by the issue requests above.

exec: // Echo the DID we published so /v1/keys/resolve can pick it up via
// {{lastPublishedDid}}. For did:key publish the route doesn't echo the
// DID directly; fall back to the request-body issuerDid the user sent.

request.description:
Publish the issuer's signing key (defaults to the loaded did:key from `{{issuerDid}}`) to the DeDi `opencred-key-registry` so verifiers can resolve it without a separate registrar. OpenCred writes **one record per key** (record name = slug of `DID#fragment`); the W3C did.json is carried as an optional immutable `document` snapshot on each key record. There is no separate `did-documents` registry.

**Body shape:** `{ did, document?, namespace?, hostDidDocument? }`.
- did:key — `{ "did": "..." }` is sufficient. The server drops `document` for did:key (the doc is derivable from the DID).
- did:web — pass `document` (the full DID Document) and set `hostDidDocument: true` to embed the did.json snapshot on the key records.

**On 409 `DEDI_RECORD_EXISTS`**: the key is already published — switch to **POST /v1/keys/resolve** below to fetch the existing record. The error response carries a `hint` pointing you there.

The `rejectKeyMaterial` defense-in-depth guard runs on the body — a `privateKey` field, or any string starting with `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`, fails 400 before anything reaches DeDi.

**Returns** `{ published, recordName, namespace, keyId, didDocumentStored }` (`didDocumentStored` is true when the did.json snapshot was embedded). `503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set.

The post-test script saves the issuer DID into `{{lastPublishedDid}}` so the resolve request below picks it up automatically.

Full did:web publish with the document body the adapter needs. Use this form when your issuer runs as did:web (`OPENCRED_ISSUER_DID_METHOD=web` + `OPENCRED_ISSUER_DOMAIN=<your-domain>`). The server writes one record per key into `opencred-key-registry` and, when `hostDidDocument: true`, embeds the did.json as an immutable `document` snapshot on those key records.

This is the manual equivalent of `OPENCRED_AUTO_PUBLISH_KEY=true` (or `OPENCRED_DEDI_HOST_DID_DOC=true`, which also embeds the did.json snapshot) — those flags publish the same keys at container startup automatically. If you set either flag and restart, you can skip this request entirely; `POST /v1/keys/resolve` returns the key record and `GET /v1/keys/did-document` returns the projected did.json.

**Body shape** mirrors the W3C DID Core document produced by `packages/did/src/did-web.ts:59` (`generateDidWebDocument`): one `verificationMethod` entry with the issuer's `publicKeyJwk`, `assertionMethod` pointing at that entry. The verification-method ID is `did:web:<domain>#key-0` (since v1.6.1 the signer's `kid` matches this exact ID, so JWTs verify against this document).

Replace `bootcamp.example.org` with your own domain and `<paste-x>` / `<paste-y>` with the P-256 public-key JWK coordinates from `GET /v1/keys`.

**Path B vs Path A**: this request publishes the keys (and optional did.json snapshot) to **DeDi only**. Non-DeDi verifiers walking `https://<your-domain>/.well-known/did.json` will still see a 404 unless you ALSO upload the same JSON to your domain (Path A — the canonical did:web setup). See `docs/concepts/dids.md#publishing-your-didweb-did-document` for the trade-off.

request.description:
Resolve a signing-key record from the DeDi `opencred-key-registry`. POST (not GET) so DIDs containing colons or slashes don't have to be URL-encoded.

**Where this looks**: DeDi only. This endpoint queries `/dedi/lookup/{namespace}/opencred-key-registry/{record}` on the configured DeDi instance (record name = slug of `DID#fragment`). It does **not** walk the canonical `https://<domain>/.well-known/did.json` URL — if you self-host a did:web document on your domain (Path A in the bootcamp), this endpoint will return 404 unless you also publish it to DeDi (Path B). For end-to-end verification of self-hosted did:web documents, use `POST /v1/credentials/verify` or the `@opencred/verify` SDK, which walks the canonical HTTPS URL first.

**Returns the bare key record** `{ keyId, controllerDid, algorithm, publicKeyJwk, purpose, status, document?, proof? }`, where `status` is `"active"`, `"rotated"`, or `"revoked"`. `document` (the did.json snapshot) is present only when it was hosted at publish/rotate time; `proof` (CORD-blockchain anchor metadata) is present when DeDi anchored the record on-chain. For the grouped did.json projected from these per-key snapshots, call `GET /v1/keys/did-document` (returns `{ did, document, source }`).

**Auto-threading**: pre-request script picks `{{lastPublishedDid}}` (set by the publish request above) if available, otherwise falls back to `{{issuerDid}}`. So a click-chain `Inspect → GET /v1/keys` → `Publish` → `Resolve` works without manual variable copying.

503 if DeDi isn't configured.

Rotate the active signer's did:web key. The DID stays stable; OpenCred writes a **new key record** into `opencred-key-registry` for the new key and marks the prior key's record `status: "rotated"`. Already-issued credentials continue to verify against the prior key — its record is retained (not deleted) and the verifier matches by `kid` from the JWT header (`packages/verification/src/vc-jwt.ts:179-213` iterates `verificationMethod[]` and picks the entry whose `id` matches the JWT's `kid`). New credentials carry the new `kid`. This is the **kid-continuity guarantee** that makes rotation safe for production did:web.

**Scope**: did:web only. did:key rotation produces a new DID — regenerate the signing key instead (the old key's record advances to `status: "rotated"`).

**Body**: `{ newKeyIndex, currentDidDocument?, hostDidDocument? }`. The rotation target is derived from the active signer — no `did` field. Set `hostDidDocument: true` to re-embed the regenerated did.json snapshot on the key records.

**Workflow**:
1. Stop the OpenCred container.
2. Swap `OPENCRED_KEY_PATH` to the new key file.
3. Restart the container.
4. Hit this endpoint.

**Response**: `{ rotated, did, currentKeyId, newKeyIndex, retired, didDocument, didDocumentStored }` — `retired` is the old key's `SetKeyStatusResult` and `didDocumentStored` is true when the snapshot was re-embedded.

**Errors**:
- `400 KEY_METHOD_MISMATCH` — active issuer is did:key (use the regenerate flow instead).
- `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — signer doesn't expose `publicKeyJwk` (KMS-backed signers not yet supported).
- `404 DEDI_CLIENT_ERROR` — key has no existing DeDi record (call `/v1/keys/publish` first).
- `503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` — DeDi env vars not set.

**Concurrency**: last-writer-wins. The per-key `setKeyStatus` write carries no `If-Match`/`version` CAS, so simultaneous lifecycle writes against the same key can race — see `docs/decisions/dedi-key-registry-redesign.md` and D4 in `docs/decisions/dedi-integration-open-questions.md`.

Revoke a single signing key by its `verificationMethod` (`DID#fragment`). Sets that key's record in `opencred-key-registry` to `status: "revoked"` — a terminal state. Distinct from credential revocation (`POST /v1/credentials/revoke`, which writes to `vc-revocation-registry`): this invalidates the **key**, so every credential signed under it fails verification.

**Body**: `{ verificationMethod, currentDidDocument?, hostDidDocument? }`. Set `hostDidDocument: true` to regenerate and re-embed the did.json snapshot (which drops the revoked key) on the remaining key records.

**Response**: `{ revoked: true, ...SetKeyStatusResult, didDocument, didDocumentRegenerated }` — `didDocumentRegenerated` is true when the snapshot was rebuilt without the revoked key.

`503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set. The same `rejectKeyMaterial` defense-in-depth guard runs on the body.

Return the current did.json projected from the per-key snapshots in `opencred-key-registry`. There is no separate `did-documents` registry — this rebuilds the grouped document from the active issuer's key records.

**Response**: `{ did, document, source }`.

`503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set.

Idempotently bootstrap a DeDi namespace and the four registries OpenCred needs (`vc-revocation-registry`, `opencred-key-registry`, `schema_registry`, `context_registry`). There is no separate `did-documents` registry — the did.json is carried as a snapshot on each key record in `opencred-key-registry`.

Wraps the same `dediClient.ensureRegistries(...)` helper that runs once at server startup, so you can spin up additional namespaces at runtime without restarting the container — useful for per-tenant setups.

Replace `your-namespace-id` in the body with the namespace ID issued by your DeDi operator. Unverified namespaces look like `did:web:did.cord.network:xyz`; verified ones look like `xyz.org`.

Returns `{ namespace, registries }` listing the registry names that now exist on the namespace (whether freshly created or already present).

Returns `503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED` until `OPENCRED_DEDI_*` env vars are set. The same `rejectKeyMaterial` defense-in-depth guard runs on the body.

Compute the JCS+SHA-256 revocation hash for a credential. Works **without** DeDi configured — pure hash computation. The hash is what gets published to a revocation registry.

Auto-saves the hash into `{{lastRevocationHash}}` for the revoke/status requests.
Compute hashes for many credentials at once. Returns `revocationHashes[]` keyed by `credentialId` (or a positional `index:N` token if a credential has no `id`).

Publish the hash to DeDi as revoked. Returns 503 DEDI_NOT_CONFIGURED unless `OPENCRED_DEDI_BASE_URL` (and friends) are set on the server.

**`{{lastRevocationHash}}` auto-populates from the issue request when `revocationRegistryUrl` is set** — no separate `/v1/credentials/revocation-hash` call needed for OpenCred-issued VCs. The server embeds the hash as the last URL segment of `credentialStatus.id` at issue time, and the issue request's post-test script extracts it.

You can also send `{ "credential": {...} }` and the server will hash it for you. Add `"namespace": "..."` to override the configured default.

`reason` is an optional free-text descriptor (per the DeDi canonical revoke.json schema) — typical values are short tags like `"key-compromised"`, `"superseded"`, or `"holder-request"`. When supplied, it is stored on the DeDi record and echoed by `/v1/credentials/revocation-status`.

**On 409 `DEDI_RECORD_EXISTS`** (introduced in #615): the hash is already revoked in DeDi from a prior run. The error response carries a `hint` pointing you at `/v1/credentials/revocation-status` to confirm the prior revoke landed.
Query DeDi for the current status of a hash. Same 503 if DeDi isn't wired up.

//   - a STRING       → compact token (sd-jwt-vc, or a raw vc-jwt token)

// requests' post-response scripts. We try to parse it as JSON: if

credential = stored;  // unwrapped JSON primitive — treat as string
credential = stored;  // compact JWT/SD-JWT token — send verbatim

request.description:
Render packaged outputs for a signed credential.

## What you get back

`outputs[]` always has one entry per requested `format`. Each entry has:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `format` | `qr-png` / `qr-svg` / `pdf` / `json` |
| `mimeType` | `image/png`, `image/svg+xml`, `application/pdf`, `application/json` |
| `suggestedFileName` | Slugged from credential `type` + last 8 chars of `id` |
| `encoding` | `base64` for PDF; `utf-8` for everything else |
| `data` | The actual content (string) |

**Decoding gotcha:** `qr-png` returns a `data:image/png;base64,<...>` URL string with `encoding: "utf-8"` (the base64 is *inside* the URL). The PDF returns pure base64 with `encoding: "base64"`. So:

```bash
# qr-png — strip the data-URL prefix first:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="qr-png") | .data | sub("^data:image/png;base64,"; "")' resp.json | base64 -d > qr.png

# pdf — straight base64:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="pdf")    | .data' resp.json | base64 -d > cert.pdf

# qr-svg / json — already utf-8:
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="qr-svg") | .data' resp.json > qr.svg
jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.format=="json")   | .data' resp.json > credential.json
```

## Input — works with all three proof formats

- `data-integrity` and `vc-jwt` → `credential` is a JSON-LD VC object (object literal in the body).
- `sd-jwt-vc` → `credential` is a compact `~`-separated token string (just paste the string).

For compact-token input, the server decodes the JWT payload offline (no signature check — packaging is a rendering step) to drive the PDF certificate layout, and embeds the original token verbatim in the QR code so any verifier scanning it runs a real cryptographic check.

## Customization

All fields under `customization` are optional. Common ones: `primaryColor` (hex), `issuerDisplayName` (NOT `issuerName` — that gets silently dropped), `secondaryColor`, `textColor`, `labelColor`, `backgroundColor`, `logoDataUri` (data: URI), `sealDataUri`, `footerText` (pass `""` to suppress the verification disclaimer).

A pre-request script reads `{{lastCredential}}` and sends it as either an object or a string depending on what the issue endpoint returned — no manual juggling. The static `raw` body shown here is the fallback for when you haven't run an issue request yet.

Kick off a batch issuance from CSV content. The first row is the header; subsequent rows become credentials. Returns a `jobId` you poll with the next two requests.

Capped by `OPENCRED_BATCH_ROW_LIMIT` (default 1000).
Poll batch progress: `pending` / `running` / `completed` / `failed`, plus row counts.
Once the job is `completed`, fetch the per-row signed credentials and any errors.
